properties.description:
`reflow2-mcp --remote <url>` is the local client of req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url, step 1 (2026-09-26). The agent (Claude Code, Grok Build, any MCP client) speaks stdio to it exactly as to a local reflow2; it forwards each message over HTTPS to a reflow2 somewhere else — flo2's api.flo2.io/g/<id>/mcp, or an organization's own server — and writes every reply back as ONE line.

THE KEY: `--api-key-env VAR` or `--api-key-file PATH` names where the key is; the key itself is refused on the command line (it would land in shell history). It goes out only as `Authorization: Bearer` and appears in no reply, error or log line. With neither flag, no Authorization header is sent (a server on a private network may want none). A key is refused over plain http:// to anything but this machine. A key file readable by other users draws a warning naming `chmod 600`.

HTTPS is reflow2's own (rustls with the ring provider, tokio-rustls, and the OS trust store through rustls-native-certs), used only in remote mode; nothing local changes (req:reflow2-keeps-working-entirely-on-one-machine).

FAILURES ARE ANSWERS: a refused key (401), a missing permission (403), a design that is not yours (404 with a key) and an unreachable server each come back as a JSON-RPC error naming the server and saying the design is not harmed — never a hung call. ONLY a 404 for a session id the server forgot (the MCP transport's signal) is re-joined, once, by replaying the client's own handshake; any other failure is not re-sent, because a change that timed out may already have landed.

Since step 3 (cap:one-setup-command-chooses-local-or-remote), `--remote <url>` with no key flag carries the key `reflow2-mcp setup` stored for that url's server, and no other.

NOT YET: a browser sign-in (step 2's keys came first), the pointer file, writing the export and measuring files locally (point 3 of the requirement), and a per-person writes_for for a server whose key names a client rather than a person (flo2 sets it from the token itself).
properties.name: An agent's stdio session works a design on a remote reflow2 server, named by URL, carrying a key the agent never sees
